Chapter 12: Embracing Mortality—Living with Death in Mind.
As we near the end of this journey, a quiet truth comes into focus: to truly live, you've got to learn how to face death.
Now, this isn't about giving in to fear, or getting lost in the pain of loss. Instead, it's about seeing mortality for what it is—a natural part of being human.
Sometimes, this realization hits all at once. Maybe it’s an illness, the passing of someone close, or just a sudden moment of clarity. For others, it unfolds slowly. Over time, you start to see that life is fragile, precious, and yes—finite.
Think about the woman who recovers from a serious illness. She steps back into her life with fresh eyes. Suddenly, the laughter of her kids feels brighter, the sun on her face warmer, and the simple comfort of a friend’s hand—so much more meaningful.
Knowing that her time is limited makes every moment sweeter, every experience more vivid.
And that’s why rituals of mourning, heartfelt conversations about death, and acts of remembrance matter so much.
They help us make space for what’s real. They let us honor the past, carry the memory of loved ones forward, and choose to live each day with intention.
Most of us don’t even realize how our lives are shaped by the stories we tell about death.
But when we pull mortality out of the shadows and talk about it openly—something shifts. We begin to create a culture that values life, that cherishes the bonds of love and memory.
Sure, this journey isn’t easy. There are moments filled with fear, sadness, and uncertainty.
But there’s also hope, courage, and the real possibility of healing.
